sections.heading: Proper Site Preparation for Driveways & Parking Lots
sections.body: Bellhouse Excavating prepares driveways, laneways, parking lots, and yard entrances for gravel, asphalt, concrete, or resurfacing. We shape the grade, remove unsuitable material, place granular base, and compact the surface so the finished area has better drainage and durability.
bullets: Parking lot and contractor-ready surface prep

sections.heading: When This Prep Work Is Worth Bringing Bellhouse In
sections.subheading: Best fit for surfaces that need more than a quick top-up and actually require grade correction, stable base, and proper compaction before the next layer goes down.

cards.title: Driveway rebuilds with soft spots or drainage issues
cards.body: A practical fit when an existing driveway is holding water, rutting, or breaking down because the grade and base underneath were never corrected properly.
cards.outcome: Addresses the underlying grade and base problem instead of just dressing up the surface for a short-term fix.

cards.title: Widening jobs and fresh granular base installs
cards.body: Useful when the work includes cutting back edges, importing stone, placing base in lifts, and tying new prep into an existing driveway or lane cleanly.
cards.outcome: Leaves a more uniform driving surface that is ready for gravel use or paving without patchwork transitions.

cards.title: Small parking areas and contractor-ready prep
cards.body: A strong fit for parking lots, yard entrances, and other traffic areas that need usable slopes, compacted base, and a clear handoff to the paving contractor or finish surface crew.
cards.outcome: Creates a surface that is easier for the next crew to pave, top, or finish without regrading on arrival.

sections.heading: A better driveway starts below the top layer.
sections.body: Bellhouse focuses on the base, grade, drainage, and compaction before the finished surface goes down. That is what keeps a driveway or parking area from becoming soft, rutted, or uneven soon after the work is done.

image.alt: Finished driveway base preparation tied into the road in Brantford

sections.caption: Finished driveway base preparation should leave a cleaner tie-in, stronger base, and more usable surface.

sections.heading: What Proper Base Prep Helps Prevent
sections.subheading: Most driveway and parking lot failures start with poor drainage, weak base, or rushed compaction.

items.problem: Soft spots and rutting can return quickly if unsuitable material is left under the surface.
items.solution: Bellhouse removes weak areas where needed and builds the base in a more controlled way.

items.problem: Flat or poorly shaped surfaces can hold water and break down the finished driveway.
items.solution: Grades are shaped with water movement in mind before gravel, asphalt, or concrete goes down.

items.problem: Loose base material can settle, shift, and leave the next crew correcting avoidable problems.
items.solution: Granular material is placed and compacted so the surface is ready for use or handoff.

sections.heading: What The Surface Should Be Ready For
sections.subheading: The goal is a driveway, lane, or parking area that is stable, drainable, and ready for the next step.

items.title: A stronger granular base
items.body: The surface is shaped and compacted so it can better support vehicle traffic, gravel topping, asphalt, or concrete.

items.title: Cleaner water movement
items.body: Slope, low spots, and edge transitions are handled so water is less likely to sit or wash out the surface.

items.title: A cleaner handoff
items.body: Paving, concrete, gravel topping, or continued site work can proceed from a more prepared surface.

items.question: What base material do you recommend?
items.answer: Granular A is common for many residential driveway and surface-prep projects, while Granular B may be used for deeper fills or heavier traffic areas. The right material depends on depth, drainage, use, and site conditions.

items.question: Do you prepare for asphalt paving?
items.answer: Yes. Bellhouse can prepare the grade and granular base so the paving contractor has a cleaner surface to work from.

items.question: Can you fix driveway drainage issues?
items.answer: Yes. Slope correction, ditching, base repair, and edge shaping can all be part of driveway or parking area prep when drainage is contributing to soft spots or washouts.

items.question: Can you supply the gravel too?
items.answer: Yes. Bellhouse can coordinate aggregate delivery with the grading and base-prep work so material, trucking, and machine time are aligned.
